title: ProtoMix: Augmenting Health Status Representation Learning via Prototype-based Mixup

problem.claim: Scarcity of labeled EHR data restricts the prediction power of deep models.

gap.claim: GAN- and diffusion-based augmentation methods can suffer from mode collapse under limited sample sizes and label imbalance, producing samples that fail to preserve EHR subtype structure.

contributions.claim: ProtoMix uses subtype-centroid prototypes as prior knowledge to guide synthesis of new samples.
ProtoMix uses prototype-guided mixup training to shift the decision boundary away from subtypes.
ProtoMix optimizes sampling weights across data-manifold regions and dynamically expands the training distribution with adaptive mixing coefficients.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report experimental evaluations on three real-world datasets.
The authors report that the evaluations demonstrate ProtoMix's efficacy.

narrative_sequence.summary: Deep learning is widely used for health prediction with EHR data.
Labeled-data scarcity limits prediction power, motivating data augmentation.
Existing generative augmentation methods may collapse modes and fail to preserve subtype structure.
ProtoMix uses prototypes, guided mixup, optimized manifold sampling, and adaptive mixing to synthesize training data.
The authors report evaluations on three real-world datasets demonstrating efficacy.

source_observation.claim: Prototype-guided mixing uses subtype-centroid information while varying sampling weights across data-manifold regions.

interpretation.claim: Augmentation may better preserve subtype structure when synthesis is conditioned on structure-aware representations rather than performed indiscriminately.

application.claim: For imbalanced, low-label health data, consider structure-aware augmentation guided by clinically meaningful subtype representations.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish performance across other domains, subtype definitions, imbalance levels, or evaluation settings.

unknowns: Dataset identities, sizes, labels, and subtype definitions are not specified.
Baselines, metrics, quantitative results, and statistical analyses are not specified.
Implementation details and computational requirements are not specified.
